mainTopic: איסור חל על איסור in קדשים, and an אשם תלוי when the owner learns he never sinned
overview: The amud opens by proving that with קדשים, one איסור can take effect on top of another. A ברייתא includes the אימורין in the איסור of eating קדשים while טמא, even though they are already forbidden as עולין and as חלב. רבי goes further: with קדשים, even a lighter איסור like מעילה (punished by מיתה) takes effect on a stricter one like חלב (punished by כרת). A ברייתא in which רבי שמעון says there is no פיגול or נותר in the עולין seems to contradict this. The גמרא answers that there are two traditions about רבי שמעון's view. The view that denies stacking explains כל חלב לה׳ as speaking of ולדי קדשים, where both איסורים begin at the same moment. Then the chapter ends, and a new משנה discusses an אשם תלוי whose owner learns he never sinned. That משנה compares it to an אשם ודאי, a שור הנסקל and an עגלה ערופה. The גמרא explains that רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about whether the owner truly meant to make the animal holy. A ברייתא shows how far each side's view reaches. רב ששת then begins to describe a case where רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים, and that teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא includes the altar portions in the טומאה prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: the פסוק's words אשר לה׳ come to include the אימורין, the parts burned on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the words "which belong to ה׳" come to include the אימורין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a source. It says that the איסור of eating קדשים while טמא also covers the אימורין, the parts meant for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a טמא person eating שלמים adds the words אשר לה׳. The ברייתא reads these extra words as including the אימורין. So a טמא person who eats them is חייב כרת. The next step will explain why this proves the גמרא's point.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of a קרבן (fats, kidneys and so on) that are burned on the מזבח
To include; a word in the פסוק adds something to the law
"Which belong to ה׳": the words in the פסוק that this דרשה is built on

phrases.english: As it is taught: "which belong to the Lord"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:20, the פסוק about a טמא person who eats שלמים.

phrases.english: – comes to include the sacrificial portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up the earlier claim that with קדשים, one איסור can take effect on top of another.
steps.raayaObject: That with קדשים, an איסור takes effect even where another איסור already exists
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that reads אשר לה׳ as including the אימורין in the איסור of eating while טמא

steps.title: Explaining the proof: טומאה takes effect on top of two existing prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: The אימורין already have איסור עולין, and the חלב in them already has איסור כרת. Still, the איסור טומאה takes effect on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The אימורין already carry the איסור of things that go up on the מזבח. The חלב already carries an איסור of כרת. And still the איסור of טומאה comes and takes effect on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא is a proof. The איסור טומאה lands on food that is already forbidden in two other ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אימורין were already forbidden as עולין, meaning they belong on the מזבח, and as חלב, which carries כרת. If an איסור normally cannot take effect where another one already exists, the ברייתא could not add טומאה here. Since it does, we see that with קדשים, איסור חל על איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור against eating things that are meant to go up on the מזבח
Forbidden fat; eating it is punished with כרת
Being "cut off"; a heavenly punishment for serious sins
The איסור against eating קדשים while טמא
Takes effect, lands on

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the אימורין stop being forbidden as עולין or as חלב. Those איסורים stay. The point is that the איסור טומאה is added on top of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic example showing that with קדשים, a new איסור can land on food that is already forbidden.

phrases.english: And sacrificial portions already stand under the prohibition of items that ascend the altar,
and the forbidden fat already stands under a prohibition of karet,
and yet the prohibition of impurity comes and takes effect on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: איסור חל על איסור with קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The איסור טומאה lands on אימורין that already carry איסור עולין and איסור חלב

steps.title: רבי lets even a lighter prohibition take effect with קדשים
steps.stepSummary: In general, רבי holds that איסור חל על איסור only when the stricter איסור comes on top of a lighter one. With קדשים, though, he lets even a lighter איסור take effect on a stricter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is so. רבי holds that one איסור takes effect on another איסור. But that is only when a strict איסור comes onto a light one. A light איסור does not take effect where the existing איסור is strict. Yet with קדשים we heard him say that even a light איסור takes effect on a strict one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second support (תדע) to show that קדשים get special treatment. This step makes the claim, and the next step gives the actual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's general rule has a limit: only a stricter איסור can take effect on top of a lighter one. With קדשים, he drops even that limit. This shows that קדשים are a special area where איסורים stack more easily than usual.

keyTerms.meaning: "Know that it is so": brings extra support for a claim
A second איסור takes effect where one already exists
A strict (heavier) איסור
A light (less severe) איסור
Holy items, especially קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: There are two levels here. רבי's general rule allows a strict איסור on top of a light one. Only with קדשים does he also allow a light איסור on top of a strict one.

phrases.english: Know that it is so,
since Rabbi holds
that a prohibition takes effect where a prohibition exists,
but this applies only to
phrases.notes: Many versions leave out the word in round brackets; read it simply as "but this applies only."

phrases.english: a severe prohibition on a lenient prohibition,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִיסּוּר קַל חָל עַל אִיסּוּר
phrases.english: but a lenient prohibition taking effect on a prohibition
when that one is a severe prohibition – no.
Yet regarding sacrificial items we heard him say:

phrases.aramaic: אִיסּוּר קַל עַל אִיסּוּר חָמוּר נָמֵי חָיֵיל,
phrases.english: a lenient prohibition also takes effect on a severe prohibition,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second support, from רבי's view, that קדשים are special when it comes to stacking איסורים.
steps.raayaObject: קדשים are a special area where איסורים stack more easily
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's position that with קדשים, even a light איסור takes effect on a strict one

steps.title: The case: מעילה takes effect on top of the כרת of קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The source for רבי's view: for רבי, מעילה is punished by מיתה, which is lighter, while קדשים carry כרת, which is stricter. Still, מעילה takes effect on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the איסור of מעילה is light, punished by מיתה. The איסור of קדשים is strict, punished by כרת. And still the איסור of מיתה comes and takes effect on the איסור of כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case that shows רבי's view about קדשים: מעילה landing on top of the כרת of קדשים. The next step quotes the ברייתא this comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מיתה בידי שמים is a lighter punishment than כרת. Even so, the איסור of מעילה takes effect on קדשים that are already forbidden under כרת. So with קדשים, a light איסור lands on a strict one.

keyTerms.meaning: Using הקדש (holy property) for one's own benefit
Death at the hands of Heaven, a lighter punishment than כרת

steps.whatToRemember: With קדשים, איסורים stack. איסור טומאה takes effect on אימורין that are already forbidden, and for רבי even a light איסור like מעילה (מיתה) takes effect on a strict one like קדשים (כרת).

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא אִיסּוּר מְעִילָה קַל הוּא – מִיתָה,
phrases.english: For the prohibition of misuse of consecrated property is lenient – death,
phrases.notes: Meaning death at the hands of Heaven, which is lighter than כרת.

phrases.english: and the prohibition of sacrificial meat is a severe prohibition – karet,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָתֵי אִיסּוּר מִיתָה חָיֵיל עַל אִיסּוּר כָּרֵת.
phrases.english: and yet the prohibition punishable by death comes and takes effect on the prohibition punishable by karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual case behind the claim about רבי in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: Even a light איסור takes effect on a strict one with קדשים
steps.raayaSupportSource: מעילה (מיתה) takes effect on קדשים that carry כרת

steps.title: The ברייתא: all the fat is for ה׳, so the אימורין get מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from כל חלב לה׳ that the altar parts of קדשים קלים are included in the laws of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, "All the fat is ה׳'s" comes to include the altar portions of lower-holiness offerings in the law of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the actual ברייתא that serves as the source for רבי's view mentioned in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat of קדשים קלים normally belongs to the owners, so it has no מעילה. The פסוק teaches that the fats burned on the מזבח, the אימורין, do belong to ה׳, so using them brings מעילה. This sets up the inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח, mainly the fats
Offerings of lower holiness, such as שלמים
To include; the פסוק adds a case
Misusing הקדש property for personal benefit

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי says:
"All the fat is the Lord's"
comes to include the altar portions of lesser-sanctity offerings in the law of misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא that step 4 relied on for רבי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That in קדשים, a lighter איסור can take effect on a stricter one
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: רבי reads כל חלב לה׳ as including אימורי קדשים קלים in מעילה

steps.title: Lighter מעילה takes effect on stricter חלב, so קדשים are different
steps.stepSummary: מעילה carries מיתה and חלב carries כרת, yet מעילה still takes effect. So for קדשים the פסוק shows that one איסור can take effect on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: And מעילה is an איסור of מיתה, yet it takes effect on the איסור of חלב, which is an איסור of כרת. Learn from this: with קדשים, the פסוק revealed the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the conclusion from the ברייתא: with קדשים, an איסור can take effect even on top of a stricter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a lighter איסור cannot take effect on a stricter one. Here the fats already carry the כרת of חלב, and still the lighter מעילה, punished only by מיתה, applies to them. Since a פסוק says so, we see that קדשים follow a special rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin punished by death from Heaven, lighter than כרת
A sin punished by כרת, spiritual cutting off
Takes effect, lands on
Learn from this; a conclusion
The פסוק revealed it, showing a special rule

steps.whatToRemember: With קדשים, a פסוק shows that an איסור can take effect on another איסור, even a lighter one on a stricter one.

phrases.english: And misuse is a prohibition punishable by death,
phrases.notes: Death here means from Heaven, not by a court.

phrases.english: and yet it takes effect on the prohibition of forbidden fat,
which is a prohibition punishable by כרת.
Learn from this: with consecrated items, the verse revealed the rule.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק showed that in קדשים, one איסור can land on another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In קדשים, איסור חל על איסור, as the תורה revealed through מעילה applying to חלב.

steps.title: רבי שמעון says there is no פיגול or נותר in the altar parts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון saying that פיגול and נותר do not apply to the parts that go up on the מזבח. That suggests that even in קדשים, one איסור does not land on another.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: there is no פיגול in the parts that go up on the מזבח, and there is no נותר in the parts that go up on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that רבי שמעון holds איסור חל על איסור in קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The altar parts already carry an איסור, the חלב in them and their status as parts for the מזבח. If רבי שמעון holds that פיגול and נותר do not take effect on them, then in his view even with קדשים a new איסור does not land on an existing one. That clashes with the idea that קדשים are special.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן offered with the intent to eat it after its proper time; eating it is forbidden
Leftover sacrificial meat past its time limit; eating it is forbidden
The parts that go up onto the מזבח to be burned

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא that רבי שמעון says:
There is no פיגול in the parts that ascend the altar,
and there is no נותר in the parts that ascend the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of step 6 as it applies to רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that in קדשים, איסור חל על איסור, used to explain רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rules that פיגול and נותר do not apply to the altar parts, which are already forbidden. That shows he holds no איסור חל על איסור even with קדשים.

steps.title: תנאים argue about what רבי שמעון holds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two traditions about רבי שמעון. One says that in קדשים an איסור lands on another, and one says that even in קדשים it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a dispute between תנאים about רבי שמעון's view. Some say: in קדשים, an איסור takes effect on an איסור. And some say: even in קדשים, an איסור does not take effect on an איסור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by saying that different תנאים reported רבי שמעון's view differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not force the two sources to agree. The view that in קדשים an איסור does land on another fits our משנה and the derivation above. The ברייתא about פיגול and נותר follows the other tradition, which says that even in קדשים it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
According to, in the view of
One prohibition takes effect on top of an existing one

steps.whatToRemember: There are two traditions about רבי שמעון. In one, קדשים are an exception and איסור חל על איסור. In the other, even in קדשים, אין איסור חל על איסור.
steps.confusionAlert: The dispute here is not between רבי שמעון and other sages. It is between later תנאים who reported רבי שמעון's own opinion in two different ways.

phrases.english: Rather, it is a dispute between תנאים,
about the opinion of רבי שמעון,
for some say:
with consecrated items, a prohibition takes effect on a prohibition,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּקָדָשִׁים נָמֵי אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: even with consecrated items, a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute among תנאים: two different traditions about the same sage's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון had only one view, so the two sources contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are two traditions about רבי שמעון. The משנה follows one and the ברייתא about פיגול and נותר follows the other.

steps.title: What does the other view do with the verse about all the fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the view that says one איסור never lands on another, even in קדשים, how it explains כל חלב לה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says that even in קדשים one איסור does not take effect on another איסור, what does he do with the פסוק ״כל חלב לה׳״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second tradition from step 8. If one איסור can never land on another, what does that view learn from the פסוק כל חלב לה׳?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, רבי used כל חלב לה׳ to show that מעילה takes effect on the altar fats of קדשים קלים, even though חלב is already forbidden. That looks like one איסור landing on another. So the view that denies this in קדשים has to explain what the פסוק is about.

keyTerms.meaning: A second prohibition cannot take effect on something that is already forbidden
What does he do with it? Meaning: how does he explain this source?
Forbidden fat of an animal; on a קרבן, it is the part burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And according to the one who says:
even with sacrificial items
a prohibition does not take effect on another prohibition,
"All the fat is to ה׳"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:16. This is the פסוק from step 5.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּקָדָשִׁים נָמֵי אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר כׇּל חֵלֶב לַה׳ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the second tradition of רבי שמעון from step 8 and tests it against the פסוק from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that even in קדשים one איסור does not take effect on another.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק כל חלב לה׳ seems to show מעילה taking effect on forbidden חלב. That view needs another explanation for the פסוק, or the פסוק goes against it.

steps.title: The verse is about offspring of sacrificial animals, where both prohibitions start together
steps.stepSummary: That view says the פסוק speaks of ולדי קדשים, which become holy at birth, so the חלב איסור and the מעילה איסור begin at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explains the פסוק as talking about the offspring of קדשים. This view holds that offspring of קדשים are holy from the moment they come into being. So both איסורים, חלב and מעילה, come at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this view reads כל חלב לה׳ as speaking of animals born to קדשים. In that case the two איסורים start together, so neither one has to land on top of the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule אין איסור חל על איסור only blocks a second איסור from landing on something already forbidden. With ולדי קדשים, the animal is holy from the start, and its חלב becomes forbidden at the same moment. Since both איסורים begin together, the פסוק no longer proves that one איסור can land on another.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring born to consecrated animals
At the moment they come into being
They come together, at the same time

steps.whatToRemember: For the view that אין איסור חל על איסור even in קדשים, כל חלב לה׳ speaks of ולדי קדשים, where קדושה and the חלב איסור start together. So the פסוק is not a case of one איסור landing on another.

phrases.english: He applies it to the offspring of sacrificial animals,
since they hold:
offspring of sacrificial animals are holy from the moment they come into being,
so the two of them come together.
phrases.notes: "The two of them" means the חלב איסור and the מעילה איסור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the פסוק to a specific case (ולדי קדשים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to describe מעילה landing on חלב that was already forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is about ולדי קדשים, where both איסורים start at the same moment, so it does not show one איסור landing on another.

steps.title: הדרן: closing פרק דם שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק דם שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק דם שחיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter called דם שחיטה. It is a closing formula, not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said at the end of every פרק. It shows that the discussion of איסור חל על איסור is finished and a new topic is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter of slaughter blood

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the last answer in step 10.

steps.title: An אשם תלוי when the owner learns he never sinned
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: if a person brought an אשם תלוי and found out he never sinned, and the animal was not yet slaughtered, רבי מאיר says it goes back to graze with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone brings an אשם תלוי and then finds out he did not sin. If this happened before the animal was slaughtered, it goes out and grazes with the flock. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. A person brought an אשם תלוי because he was unsure whether he sinned, and then he learned he did not sin at all. רבי מאיר rules that if the animal was not yet slaughtered, it goes back to being an ordinary animal in the flock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם תלוי is brought only because of a doubt about a sin. רבי מאיר holds that once it is clear there was no sin, the animal was set aside for nothing, so it is not holy and simply returns to the flock. The משנה will go on to give other opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'hanging' guilt offering, brought when a person is unsure whether he did a sin that needs a חטאת
Was slaughtered
It grazes with the flock, meaning it is treated as an ordinary animal

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with an animal that becomes disqualified and must wait for a blemish. רבי מאיר is saying the animal was never truly holy, so it simply goes back to the flock.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who brings a provisional guilt offering,
and it became known to him that he did not sin,
if it was before it was slaughtered,
it goes out and grazes with the flock,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמֵּבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי וְנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter right after the הדרן in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, an אשם תלוי whose owner learns before slaughter that he did not sin is not holy and returns to graze with the flock.

steps.title: חכמים: let it graze until blemished, then sell it
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. The animal grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and the money goes to נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Rabbis say: it should graze until it gets a blemish, then be sold, and its money goes to voluntary offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second opinion about an אשם תלוי that was not yet slaughtered when the owner learned he never sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said the animal just goes back to the flock as a regular animal. חכמים hold it still has some holiness, so it cannot simply go free. It has to wait for a blemish, be sold, and the money is used for voluntary offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Gets a blemish (a מום) that makes it unfit to be offered
It is sold
Its money, the price it sells for (not 'its blood' here)
Voluntary offerings; here, the fund used to buy them

steps.confusionAlert: In this line דָּמָיו means 'its money,' not 'its blood.' Later in the משנה, the word הַדָּם does mean the blood of the offering.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
It should graze until it gets a blemish
and it should be sold, and its money goes to voluntary offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opinion that argues with רבי מאיר in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unslaughtered אשם תלוי of someone who learns he did not sin grazes until blemished, is sold, and its money goes to נדבה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: it is still offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says the animal should be offered anyway, since it can count for a different sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: it should be offered, because if it does not come for this sin, it comes for another sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third opinion: the animal is brought as an offering after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reasons that the offering is not wasted. Even if the owner did not commit this sin, it can cover some other unknown sin. So nothing needs to be sold or released.

keyTerms.meaning: It is offered on the מזבח
A different sin, one the person may have done without knowing

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it should be offered,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא זֶה –
phrases.english: for if it does not come for this sin,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי הוּא בָּא עַל חֵטְא אַחֵר.
phrases.english: it comes for another sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third opinion beside רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אשם תלוי is still offered, because it can atone for some other sin.
steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions when he learns before שחיטה that he never sinned: רבי מאיר says it goes back to the flock. חכמים say it grazes until blemished and its money goes to נדבה. רבי אליעזר says it is offered.

steps.title: Finding out after slaughter or after the blood is sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: If he finds out after שחיטה, the blood is poured out and the meat is burned. If he finds out after the blood is sprinkled, the meat is eaten. רבי יוסי says that even if the blood is still in the cup, it is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found out after it was slaughtered, the blood is poured out and the meat goes to the place of burning. If the blood was already sprinkled and the meat is still there, it is eaten. רבי יוסי says: even if the blood is still in the cup, it is sprinkled and the meat is eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to later stages: what happens to the אשם תלוי if he finds out after it was slaughtered, or after its blood was sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After שחיטה but before sprinkling, the offering is treated as unfit: its blood is poured out and its meat is burned. Once the blood was sprinkled, the offering is already done, so the meat is eaten like any other offering. רבי יוסי moves that point earlier: even blood still sitting in the cup may be sprinkled.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood is poured out, not put on the מזבח
The place where unfit sacred meat is burned
The blood was sprinkled on the מזבח
The cup the blood is collected in after שחיטה

phrases.english: If he found out after it was slaughtered
phrases.notes: He found out that he never sinned at all.

phrases.english: the blood is poured out,
and the meat goes out to the place of burning.
If the blood was sprinkled and the meat is still there, it is eaten.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ הַדָּם בַּכּוֹס –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: even if the blood is still in the cup,
it is sprinkled, and the meat is eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the same אשם תלוי case to later stages of the offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After שחיטה: pour out the blood and burn the meat. After sprinkling: eat the meat. רבי יוסי: even blood in the cup is sprinkled and the meat eaten.

steps.title: An אשם ודאי works differently
steps.stepSummary: For an אשם ודאי: before שחיטה it goes back to the flock, after שחיטה it is buried, and after the blood is sprinkled the meat is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: A definite guilt offering is not like this. Before it is slaughtered, it goes out and grazes with the flock. After it is slaughtered, it is buried. If the blood was sprinkled, the meat goes out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares the אשם תלוי to an אשם ודאי and shows the rules are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אשם ודאי is brought for a sin the person is sure he did. So if it turns out there was no sin, it was never really holy: before שחיטה it is just a regular animal, and after שחיטה it is buried. Even after the blood is sprinkled, the meat is not eaten but burned, which is the opposite of the אשם תלוי.

keyTerms.meaning: A guilt offering brought for a sin the person knows for sure he did
It is not like this; the rule is different
It is buried
The flock

steps.confusionAlert: After the blood is sprinkled, an אשם תלוי is eaten but an אשם ודאי is burned. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: A definite guilt offering is not like this:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁחַט – יֵצֵא וְיִרְעֶה בָּעֵדֶר.
phrases.english: before it is slaughtered, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
After it is slaughtered, it is buried.

phrases.aramaic: נִזְרַק הַדָּם – הַבָּשָׂר יֵצֵא לְבֵית הַשְּׂרֵיפָה.
phrases.english: If the blood was sprinkled, the meat goes out to the place of burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the אשם ודאי to the אשם תלוי rules in steps 12 to 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם ודאי with no real sin: before שחיטה it goes to the flock, after שחיטה it is buried, and after sprinkling its meat is burned.

steps.title: A שור הנסקל, an ox sentenced to stoning
steps.stepSummary: A שור הנסקל is also different. If the ox turns out innocent before stoning, it goes back to the flock. If it was already stoned, one may benefit from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox that is stoned is not like this. Before it is stoned, it goes out and grazes with the flock. After it is stoned, one may benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another comparison: an ox sentenced to stoning that turns out not to deserve it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one may not benefit from a שור הנסקל. But if the sentence turns out to be a mistake, the ox never had that status. So before stoning it simply goes free, and even after stoning its body is permitted for benefit.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox sentenced to be stoned, for example for killing a person
Permitted to benefit from, for example selling its hide or meat

steps.whatToRemember: When the reason for the animal's status turns out false, the אשם תלוי, the אשם ודאי and the שור הנסקל each get their own rule. After שחיטה, the אשם תלוי is treated as a real קרבן, while the אשם ודאי is not. Before שחיטה, רבי מאיר sends the אשם תלוי back to the flock.

phrases.english: An ox that is stoned is not like this:
phrases.notes: It turns out the ox never deserved the sentence, for example because the witnesses were lying.

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִסְקָל – יֵצֵא וְיִרְעֶה בָּעֵדֶר.
phrases.english: before it is stoned, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
After it is stoned, one may benefit from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second comparison case after the אשם ודאי in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wrongly sentenced שור הנסקל goes to the flock before stoning, and is permitted for benefit after stoning.

steps.title: The עגלה ערופה is also different
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends with עגלה ערופה. Before its neck is broken, it goes back to the flock. After its neck is broken, it is buried, because it already atoned for the doubt it came for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עגלה ערופה is not like this. If the killer is found before its neck is broken, it goes out and grazes with the flock. Once its neck has been broken, it is buried where it is. It came for a doubt from the start, so it atoned for that doubt and its job is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more case that works differently: the עגלה ערופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה was brought only because nobody knew who the killer was. Once its neck is broken, it has already done its job of atoning for that doubt. Finding the killer later does not undo it, so the animal stays forbidden and is buried.

keyTerms.meaning: The heifer whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
Its neck was broken
It is buried in its place
It atoned for its doubt

steps.whatToRemember: An animal that comes because of a doubt has finished its job once the main act is done. Learning the truth afterward does not change that.

phrases.english: The heifer whose neck is broken is not like this:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁלֹּא נֶעֶרְפָה – תֵּצֵא וְתִרְעֶה בָּעֵדֶר,
phrases.english: before its neck was broken, it goes out and grazes in the flock;
phrases.notes: The case is that the killer turned out to be found. That is what makes the heifer no longer needed.

phrases.english: once its neck was broken, it is buried in its place,
because it came for a doubt from the start;
it atoned for its doubt and went on its way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final contrasting case to the list that began with the שור הנסקל in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עגלה ערופה goes back to the flock if the killer is found before its neck is broken. Afterward it is buried, since it already atoned for the doubt.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins and asks what רבי מאיר and חכמים are really arguing about in the case of the אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What are they arguing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion with a question. It is setting up the next step, which explains the reasoning behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in the משנה, רבי מאיר said the animal becomes ordinary if the owner learns he did not sin. חכמים said it stays holy and must graze until it gets a blemish. The גמרא wants the reason behind each view, not just the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What are they arguing about?

phrases.english: GEMARA: About what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means רבי מאיר and חכמים, about the animal set aside as an אשם תלוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the משנה's argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind the argument about whether an אשם תלוי stays holy once the owner learns he did not sin.

steps.title: Did he really mean to make it holy?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that someone who turns out not to need the animal never truly made it holy. חכמים say his worried conscience made him fully commit to making it holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: since it turns out he does not need it, he did not really make it holy. חכמים hold: because his heart was troubling him, he made up his mind completely and made it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving the reasoning of each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is about what the owner had in mind when he set the animal aside. רבי מאיר says he only meant it for the case that he really needs it, so if he doesn't, the holiness falls away. חכמים say his guilty feeling made him commit without conditions, so the holiness stays.

keyTerms.meaning: He doesn't need it
Makes an animal holy, setting it aside for the מקדש
His heart troubles him; a guilty conscience
He makes up his mind completely

steps.whyThisMatters: The argument turns out to be about a person's state of mind when he sets something aside as holy, not about the animal itself.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, לָא מַקְדֵּישׁ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: since he does not need it, he does not consecrate it.
And the Rabbis hold:
since his heart strikes him,
phrases.notes: His worry that he might have sinned keeps bothering him.

phrases.english: he resolves fully and consecrates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר: the holiness depends on actually needing the animal. חכמים: his guilty conscience led him to make it fully holy with no conditions.

steps.title: They argue in both cases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי מאיר and חכמים argue both when the owner learns he sinned and when he learns he did not sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: whether he found out that he sinned or found out that he did not sin, רבי מאיר and חכמים argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the argument covers two different cases. It is setting up the next two steps, which explain why both cases are mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about a man who learned he did not sin. The ברייתא adds a second case: he learned he really did sin, so now he needs a חטאת instead of the אשם תלוי. The argument applies there too.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
Whether... or...
It became known to him

phrases.english: It was taught: whether it became known to him that he sinned
or it became known to him that he did not sin,
Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the argument explained in step 20 to a second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים applies both when he learns he sinned and when he learns he did not sin.

steps.title: How far רבי מאיר goes
steps.stepSummary: The case where he learns he sinned shows how far רבי מאיר goes. Even then the animal becomes ordinary, because when he set it aside he did not know for sure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue in the case where he learned he sinned to show you the strength of רבי מאיר's view. Even though he now knows he sinned, since he did not know at the time he set the animal aside, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא bothered to mention the case where he learned he sinned: it shows the strength of רבי מאיר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that if he really did sin, the animal was set aside for a real sin and should stay holy. רבי מאיר says no. He set it aside as an אשם תלוי for a doubt, and now he needs a חטאת instead, so the animal is not needed and becomes ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength of his view
Even though
At the time he set it aside
A guilt offering brought when one is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: In the case where it became known to him that he sinned,
it is to show you the strength of Rabbi Meir's view,
that even though he knows that he sinned,
since at the time that he set it aside
he did not know,
phrases.notes: The square bracket opens here and closes in the next step. The words inside are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: it shall go out and graze in the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁחָטָא – לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחוֹ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first case listed in the ברייתא of step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, even if he learns he did sin, the animal becomes ordinary, since he did not know for sure when he set it aside.

steps.title: How far חכמים go
steps.stepSummary: The case where he learns he did not sin shows how far חכמים go. Even though there was no sin at all, the animal stays holy, because his guilty conscience made him fully commit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue in the case where he learned he did not sin to show you the strength of חכמים' view. Even though he did not sin, since he did not know at the time he set it aside, his heart was troubling him. So he made up his mind completely and made it holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא mentioned the case where he learned he did not sin: it shows the strength of חכמים' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there was no sin at all, it seems most obvious that the animal was never needed. Still, חכמים say it stays holy. What counts is how he felt when he set it aside: he was worried, so he committed fully.

keyTerms.meaning: The strength of חכמים' view
Therefore

steps.whatToRemember: Each side's view is strongest in a different case. רבי מאיר's is strongest when he did sin and the animal still becomes ordinary. חכמים' is strongest when he did not sin and the animal still stays holy.

phrases.english: And in the case where it became known to him that he did not sin,
it is to show you the strength of the Rabbis' view,
that even though he did not sin,
since at the time that he set it aside he did not know,
his heart was striking him;
therefore he resolved fully and consecrated it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁלֹּא חָטָא – לְהוֹדִיעֲךָ כֹּחָן דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second case listed in the ברייתא, parallel to step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, even if he learns he did not sin at all, the animal stays holy, because his guilty conscience made him fully commit.

steps.title: רב ששת: רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins a new statement: there is a situation where רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת starts a new teaching saying that רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים in some case. This line is a setup, and the גמרא will explain which case it means in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we saw only how far apart רבי מאיר and חכמים are. רב ששת now signals that their argument has a limit, because in at least one situation רבי מאיר takes the same view as חכמים. To understand the limit, we must wait for the case he describes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees or concedes. One side in a מחלוקת accepts the other side's view in a certain case.
The Sages, the group that argues with רבי מאיר here.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי מאיר is giving up his whole opinion. 'מודה' here means he agrees only in one specific case, and the rest of the מחלוקת stays in place.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Rabbi Meir concedes to the Rabbis

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי מֵאִיר לַחֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא showed how far each side goes, רב ששת begins to mark a limit on רבי מאיר's view: a case where he agrees with חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a case where רבי מאיר agrees with חכמים. The case itself is spelled out in the next part of the גמרא.
